questions.question: Why do AI coding agents struggle in large monorepos?
questions.answer_summary: LLM context windows (100k-2M tokens) are dwarfed by enterprise monorepos spanning tens of millions of tokens, and relevance can't be determined without traversing a dependency graph the agent hasn't loaded.

questions.question: What is 'interface hallucination' in a monorepo context?
questions.answer_summary: An agent generates syntactically correct code calling a method signature that was renamed elsewhere in a shared library months earlier, because it infers from stale training data rather than the current interface.

questions.question: Is there a practical file-count ceiling before an AI agent's indexing degrades?
questions.answer_summary: One analysis cites roughly 2,500 files as the practical ceiling for naive context-stuffing before tool indexing quality visibly degrades.

questions.question: Why does Cursor create files in the wrong folder in a monorepo/workspace setup?
questions.answer_summary: Developers report Cursor bypassing intended folder structures (e.g., an apps/ folder) and creating files at the workspace root instead of the correct subdirectory, even after trying .cursorignore and .mdc rule files.

questions.question: Can something as simple as an emoji in a folder name break monorepo indexing?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — one user found that an emoji in a code-workspace folder name prevented that folder from being indexed at all; removing the emoji fixed indexing.

questions.question: Does an AI agent break in a polyrepo the same way it does in a monorepo?
questions.answer_summary: In a polyrepo setup an agent is blind to everything outside the current repo, so it guesses at interfaces and invents contracts that don't match, breaking integration — a related but distinct failure mode from monorepo context overload.

questions.question: How should teams scope an AI agent session in a large monorepo?
questions.answer_summary: The most reliable approach is scoping the agent session to the specific package being worked on (e.g., opening a subdirectory directly) rather than pointing it at the whole repo root.

questions.question: Does an AI assistant follow a codebase's existing naming/export conventions in a monorepo?
questions.answer_summary: Not reliably — one developer found Claude generated a React component using default exports and different state-naming conventions than the monorepo's established pattern (named exports, custom hooks), and then applied its own convention inconsistently across the repo.

questions.question: Do CLAUDE.md-style rule files actually help agents respect monorepo boundaries?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — describing repository structure in CLAUDE.md or .cursor/rules helps the AI understand package boundaries and avoid breaking shared code, though it isn't foolproof.

questions.question: Are bigger context windows the real fix for monorepo AI problems?
questions.answer_summary: No — teams getting reliable cross-service agent results aren't relying on bigger context windows; they're building navigation infrastructure (indexing, dependency graphs, RAG) that lets agents find the right code precisely.

questions.question: Is monorepo adoption increasing specifically because of AI coding tools?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — commentary suggests monorepos are being reconsidered/adopted specifically because tools like Cursor and Claude Code get native cross-package visibility inside one repo that they lack across separate repos.
